result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is green (7 pass, 0 fail), and I verified the endpoint end to end out of band: healthy → `200 {"status":"ok","checks":{"db":{"status":"ok",...}}}`, unreachable database → `503 {"status":"error","checks":{"db":{"status":"error","message":"disk I/O error"}}}`.

I replaced the static `/health` handler with a real dependency probe. `app/Health/HealthCheck.ts` is the new check module: `probeDatabase()` resolves the connection through `getDatabase()` from `config/database.ts` and runs `sql\`select 1\`` on every call (no caching, no flag), dispatching structurally between drizzle's `run()` and `execute()` so a driver swap in `config/database.ts` needs no change here; `checkDatabase()` wraps it in a 2s timeout and converts any throw, rejection, or hang into a failed `CheckResult` instead of an exception; `runHealthChecks()` assembles the `{ status, checks: { db: { status, durationMs, message? } }, timestamp }` report with the `ok`/`error` vocabulary, and `healthStatusCode()` maps it to 200 or 503. `app/Http/Controllers/HealthController.ts` returns that report via `this.json(report, { status: healthStatusCode(report) })`, and `routes/web.ts` now points `router.get('/health', …)` at it — still unnamed, unauthenticated, and covered by the existing `exclude: ['/health']` host-authorization exemption in `src/app.ts`, which I did not touch. `tests/HealthController.test.ts` covers the live HTTP 200 path with its per-check status plus the failure mapping, the connection-cannot-open case, and that consecutive probes actually re-run the query; the pre-existing tests are unchanged.
